spec.title: Q2 FY2026 Sales Performance Review
spec.subtitle: Ref: SPR-26Q2-NAEMEA | Date: 18 July 2026 | From: VP Global Revenue Operations

sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: Q2 FY2026 closed at $84.7M in total revenue, representing 107% of quarterly target and 14% year-over-year growth. Outperformance was primarily driven by North America, which achieved 112% of plan, and by continued momentum in Core subscription products. In contrast, EMEA finished at 93% of target due to late-stage opportunity slippage and extended deal cycles in enterprise accounts. The overall pipeline coverage entering Q3 stands at 3.1x quota, though distribution and stage balance require corrective action.

sections.heading: Regional Performance Summary
sections.body: North America delivered $51.3M against a $45.8M target, fueled by strong conversion rates in the mid-funnel (Stage 2 to Stage 3 improved from 46% in Q1 to 58% in Q2). The Central and West territories led performance, particularly in healthcare and fintech verticals. EMEA closed $21.4M versus a $23.0M plan, with the UKI region experiencing an average 18-day cycle extension compared to Q1. APAC remained steady at 101% attainment, though deal sizes were smaller than forecast.

sections.heading: Product Line Analysis
sections.body: Core subscriptions generated $62.5M in bookings, exceeding plan by 11%, supported by bundled pricing incentives and improved cross-sell motions within existing accounts. Advanced Analytics add-ons underperformed at 88% of target due to delayed procurement approvals in two strategic EMEA accounts. Renewal rates for Core remained strong at 94.2%, while expansion ARR grew 9% quarter-over-quarter. Product attach rates improved in North America but declined slightly in DACH markets.

sections.heading: Loss Trends
sections.body: Mid-funnel velocity improved globally, with average time in Stage 2 decreasing from 21 days to 16 days, contributing to higher conversion into proposal stages. However, late-stage slippage increased in EMEA, where 27% of Stage 4 opportunities were pushed to Q3 compared to 14% in Q1. Overall win rate rose to 31% (up from 28%), largely attributable to disciplined qualification in North America. Loss analysis indicates pricing sensitivity and delayed security reviews as the primary drivers of competitive losses in EMEA.

sections.heading: Sales Cycle Metrics and Account Manager Productivity
sections.body: The global average sales cycle measured 74 days, down from 81 days in Q1, though EMEA enterprise cycles extended to 96 days on average. Account managers in North America achieved $1.42M in quarterly bookings per head, compared to $1.08M in EMEA. Top-quartile performers maintained pipeline coverage above 3.5x and conducted 22% more executive-level meetings than the regional average. For Q3, targeted enablement will focus on late-stage deal management, executive alignment in EMEA accounts, and structured opportunity reviews to reduce slippage.
